claim: Mechanical validity does not imply structural fidelity.
evidence: All 10 mechanically valid/evaluable rows had F1 0.1362–0.2813; exact matches were 0/10.

claim: Structural fidelity does not perfectly determine policy fidelity.
evidence: At similar low F1, P2 GPT R1 was decision-correct (0.1881) while P4b GPT R1 was decision-wrong (0.1802); this is descriptive and scenario-confounded.

claim: Generated-model planning can expose consequential world-model errors.
evidence: Both evaluable P4b GPT rows planned risky_route and incurred reference-world regret 0.375.

claim: Some structurally different models preserve the correct decision.
evidence: P2_FRAGILE_DELIVERY_GPT_R1 had F1 0.1881 but transferred pick_up with regret 0.

claim: Some mechanically valid generated models induce positive reference-world regret.
evidence: Both valid P4b GPT rows had positive regret 0.375.

claim: P4b demonstrates a safety-relevant policy error in confirmatory data.
evidence: Both evaluable P4b GPT rows select risky_route rather than safe_route; reference transferred collision probability is 0.5.

claim: Structural F1 is a sufficient proxy for downstream usefulness.
evidence: A correct zero-regret P2 row and wrong positive-regret P4b row occur at similar low F1, and the only paired F1/regret sample is N=3.
